formation.title: The Birth of the Eidgenossenschaft
formation.text:
The Swiss cantons have achieved what seemed impossible: from scattered mountain communities bound only by oaths of mutual defense, a new nation has been forged in the heart of Europe. The Confederation stands as proof that free men need not bow to any prince. But what kind of nation shall this be?

The alpine passes command the trade routes between Italy and northern Europe. The cantonal militias have shattered every army sent against them. The question is not whether Switzerland will endure, but what it will become: a fortress unto itself, or a nation whose warriors march under foreign banners for gold and glory.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We shall be a fortress; none shall cross our mountains unbidden

modifiers.name: Armed Neutrality
modifiers.text: The Swiss Confederation has chosen the path of armed neutrality, a nation that fights no foreign wars but makes itself impregnable at home. Behind mountain walls and cantonal militias, the Eidgenossen forge a republic that answers to no emperor, king, or pope.

options.text: Our pikes are for hire. Let the kings of Europe bid for our service

modifiers.name: Reisläufer Tradition
modifiers.text: The cantons have embraced their martial reputation, sending their sons to fight in the service of Europe's kings. Swiss mercenaries are the most feared infantry on the continent, and the pension gold flowing back to the alpine valleys enriches a nation of warriors.

advances.name: Letzi Fortifications
advances.text: The construction of Letzi barrier walls across alpine valleys and lake approaches, channeling invaders into prepared kill zones.

advances.name: Alpine Halberdiers
advances.text: The mountain warriors who wielded the halberd, a uniquely Swiss weapon combining axe, hook, and spike, to devastating effect against armored knights.

advances.name: Alpine Crossbowmen
advances.text: Swiss marksmen trained in the use of the crossbow amid mountain terrain, providing ranged support before the halberdiers close for the kill.

advances.name: Communal Oath
advances.text: The tradition of Eidgenossenschaft, the sworn oath of mutual defense that binds free communities together without feudal overlordship.

advances.name: Alpine Pass Trade
advances.text: Control of the great alpine passes, the Gotthard, Simplon, and Great St Bernard, that connect northern and southern Europe. The valleys along each road carry the merchants' bales by stages, from one Sust to the next.

advances.name: Legacy of Sempach
advances.text: The victory at Sempach in 1386 that transformed the Swiss from rebellious peasants into a recognized military power feared across Europe.

advances.name: Tagsatzung Tradition
advances.text: The institution of the Tagsatzung, the federal diet where cantonal delegates negotiated policy through consensus rather than command.

advances.name: Gevierthaufen Tactics
advances.text: The development of the Gevierthaufen, massive pike columns of thousands of disciplined infantrymen advancing in coordinated echelons. Every canton musters its able men and picks the Auszug, the first call, to fill the column.

advances.name: Mercenary Capitulations
advances.text: The institutionalization of mercenary service, with cantonal governments negotiating formal capitulation agreements with foreign powers.

advances.name: Swiss Textile Industry
advances.text: The flourishing textile production centered on St. Gallen, Zurich, and Basel, specializing in linen, wool, and later silk.

advances.name: Alpine Hospices
advances.text: The network of hospices maintained by monastic orders along the great alpine passes, offering shelter and care to travelers and pilgrims.

advances.name: Swiss Guard Heritage
advances.text: The prestige of Swiss military service, epitomized by the Papal Swiss Guard, the ultimate testament to Swiss martial reputation.

advances.name: Swiss Pike Warfare
advances.text: The perfection of pike square tactics that made Swiss infantry the terror of European battlefields from Grandson to Novara.

advances.name: Reisläufer Service
advances.text: The professional mercenary tradition of the Reisläufer, Swiss soldiers who hired their services to the highest bidder across Europe.

advances.name: Perpetual Peace
advances.text: The Treaty of Perpetual Peace with France in 1516, marking Switzerland's decisive turn away from wars of conquest.

event.title: The Perpetual Peace of 1516
event.text:
The disasters of the Italian Wars, the bloodbath at Marignano where Swiss pikemen fell in their thousands against French artillery, the futile sieges and broken alliances, have taught the Confederation a bitter lesson. War abroad brings glory to individuals but ruin to the state.

The Treaty of Perpetual Peace with France, signed in Fribourg in 1516, marks a turning point. Switzerland will no longer fight wars of conquest. In exchange, the French crown gains the right to recruit Swiss mercenaries, but the Confederation itself stands apart from European conflicts, its neutrality purchased not with weakness but with the demonstrated ferocity of its citizens.

options.text: Let this peace endure; our strength lies in our restraint

modifiers.name: Perpetual Peace
modifiers.text: After decades of bloodshed in Italy's wars, the Swiss have concluded a lasting peace that reshapes their place in Europe, no longer aggressors, but respected neutrals whose word carries weight precisely because they no longer draw their swords.

advances.name: Geneva Banking
advances.text: The rise of Geneva as a European financial center, building on its medieval trade fairs and Calvin's pragmatic approach to usury.

event.title: The Rise of Geneva Banking
event.text:
Since Bishop Adhémar Fabri granted Genevan bankers permission to charge interest in 1387, the city has grown into one of Europe's premier financial centers. The great trade fairs draw merchants and financiers from across the continent, and Calvin's pragmatic reinterpretation of usury laws has further loosened the constraints on commerce.

Swiss banking houses now manage the wealth of princes and merchants alike. The counting houses of Geneva, Basel, and Zurich form a financial network that spans the continent, discreet, efficient, and answerable only to their cantonal councils.

options.text: Gold flows to those who keep their promises and their silence

advances.name: Printing and Learning
advances.text: Basel's emergence as a center of printing and humanist scholarship, home to Erasmus and the great publishing houses.

advances.name: Civic Governance
advances.text: The Swiss tradition of municipal self-governance through elected town councils, establishing the foundations of democratic republicanism.

advances.name: Reformation Crossroads
advances.text: The Swiss experience of the Reformation, where Zwingli and Calvin reshaped Christianity from Zurich and Geneva, while Catholic cantons held firm.

event.title: The Swiss Reformation
event.text:
The Confederation faces its gravest internal crisis. Huldrych Zwingli in Zurich and later John Calvin in Geneva have torn apart the religious unity that bound the cantons together. Catholic and Protestant cantons eye each other with suspicion, and the Kappel Wars have already spilled blood between brothers.

Yet from this crucible of confessional strife, something unexpected emerges: a grudging tolerance born of necessity. Neither side can crush the other without destroying the Confederation itself. The Swiss must find a way to live with their differences, or perish divided.

options.text: Embrace the new learning. Let scripture and reason guide us

modifiers.name: Spirit of the Reformation
modifiers.text: The teachings of Zwingli and Calvin have swept through the Swiss cantons, bringing a new emphasis on literacy, education, and the individual's direct relationship with scripture.

options.text: Hold fast to the true faith; the old ways have served us well

modifiers.name: Counter-Reformation Zeal
modifiers.text: The Catholic cantons have rallied in defense of the old faith, strengthening their devotion and missionary efforts against the Protestant tide.

advances.name: Cantonal Sovereignty
advances.text: The principle that each canton retains sovereignty over its internal affairs, creating a uniquely decentralized form of governance.

advances.name: Watchmaking Tradition
advances.text: The establishment of Swiss watchmaking, brought by Huguenot refugees to Geneva and spread through the Jura mountains.

event.title: The Art of Precision
event.text:
Huguenot refugees fleeing persecution in France have brought their extraordinary skill in horology to Geneva, where the art of watchmaking has taken root and flourished. Swiss ateliers now produce the finest timepieces in Europe, intricate mechanisms of gears and springs that measure the hours with unprecedented accuracy.

What began as a craft for wealthy patrons is becoming an industry. The precision demanded by watchmaking drives innovation in metalwork, optics, and engineering. The Swiss reputation for meticulous craftsmanship, already established in arms and textiles, now finds its ultimate expression in the exquisite mechanisms ticking away in workshops from Geneva to Schaffhausen.

options.text: Precision is the Swiss virtue, in war, in finance, and now in craft

advances.name: Arsenal System
advances.text: The cantonal arsenal system maintaining stockpiles of weapons and equipment so every citizen can be armed within hours of a call to service.

advances.name: Swiss Musketeers
advances.text: Swiss soldiers adopting gunpowder weapons while maintaining their traditional discipline and mountain-fighting expertise.

advances.name: Swiss Civic Humanism
advances.text: The intellectual tradition combining classical republican ideals with Swiss communal governance, flourishing in Basel and Zurich.

advances.name: Cantonal Militia System
advances.text: The modernized militia system prescribed by the federal treaty, requiring each canton to maintain a standing contingent of trained soldiers.

advances.name: Helvetic Banking
advances.text: The maturation of Swiss banking from Geneva's trade fair origins into sophisticated financial institutions serving all of Europe.

advances.name: Armed Neutrality Doctrine
advances.text: The formalization of armed neutrality as Swiss state doctrine, peace through strength, defended by every citizen.

advances.name: Anti-Absolutism
advances.text: Switzerland's principled rejection of absolutist monarchy, maintaining republican traditions while Europe's kings concentrate power.

advances.name: Cheese and Dairy Trade
advances.text: The development of Swiss alpine dairy farming and cheese production into a major export industry, particularly Emmentaler and Gruyère.

advances.name: Shooting Tradition
advances.text: The Swiss tradition of communal shooting festivals and marksmanship competitions, ensuring every citizen maintains military readiness.

advances.name: Federal Constitution
advances.text: The adoption of a modern federal constitution establishing a permanent central government while preserving cantonal autonomy.

advances.name: Precision Manufacturing
advances.text: The expansion of Swiss precision craftsmanship from watchmaking into broader industrial manufacturing and engineering.

advances.name: Swiss Sharpshooters
advances.text: Elite marksmen combining the Swiss shooting tradition with modern rifled firearms, excelling in mountain warfare.

advances.name: Financial Center
advances.text: The emergence of Switzerland as Europe's preeminent financial center, built on banking discretion, political stability, and the rule of law.

advances.name: Popular Education
advances.text: The Swiss commitment to universal public education, inspired by Pestalozzi's educational philosophy, producing one of Europe's most literate populations.

advances.name: Professional Diplomacy
advances.text: Swiss expertise as neutral mediators and diplomats, building on centuries of balancing between powerful neighbors.

destiny.name: Swiss Destiny
destiny.text: The Confederation stands formed. Now choose the path that will define its legacy: a fortress of liberty and finance, or an empire built by the world's finest soldiers.

event.title: The Destiny of the Eidgenossenschaft
event.text: The Confederation is formed, but its true character remains to be determined. The cantonal delegates have sworn their oaths and the white cross flies over the alpine passes. Now the real work begins: forging a nation from free communities that must decide whether to look inward or outward, whether to build walls or march beyond them.

options.text: The oath binds us. Now let us build upon it

destiny.name: Alpine Banking Foundation
destiny.text: Consolidate control over the Swiss cantons and open the Geneva Counting House that will make the Confederation Europe's most trusted banker. Requires a Geneva Counting House in Geneva, 1,000 gold, and Geneva grown rich on its fairs.

conditions.text: We own Geneva and a Geneva Counting House stands there
We own Geneva and its development is at least 31

event.title: Foundations of Swiss Finance
event.text:
Geneva's counting house has opened its books, and the counting houses multiply. Where once the Swiss were known only for their arms, they are now gaining a reputation for something equally powerful: discretion with other people's money. Geneva's trade fairs draw merchants and financiers from across Europe, and the Swiss franc is becoming a currency of trust.

The foundation is laid. What was once a collection of mountain peasants defending their valleys is becoming a sophisticated financial state.

options.text: Trust is our currency, and we shall never debase it

destiny.name: Banking Capital of Europe
destiny.text: Transform Switzerland into the financial heart of Europe. The counting houses of Geneva, Basel, and Zurich must become indispensable to every prince and merchant on the continent. Requires books in the capital's market, 2,000 gold, high prestige, and Basel built up as a city of printers and bankers.

children.text: Books is produced in the market
Books is traded in the market

conditions.text: We own Basel and its development is at least 24

event.title: The Bankers of Europe
event.text:
Switzerland has achieved what no mountain nation was expected to achieve: it has become the banking capital of Europe. The counting houses of Geneva manage the wealth of kings. Basel's financiers underwrite the trade of nations. Zurich's discretion is legendary.

This prosperity brings a choice: invest in peaceful development and stable governance, or leverage this financial power to project Swiss prestige across the continent.

options.text: Invest in our cantons: prosperity is its own reward

modifiers.name: Peaceful Prosperity
modifiers.text: Swiss neutrality yields its greatest dividend: uninterrupted domestic development and contented cantons.

options.text: Let the world know Swiss neutrality has its price

modifiers.name: Prestigious Neutrality
modifiers.text: Swiss neutrality commands respect across Europe, though the standing army grows expensive to maintain without actual wars to justify its cost.

destiny.name: The Perpetual Republic
destiny.text: Achieve the ultimate expression of Swiss governance: a republic so stable, so prosperous, and so exact in its arts that it endures when empires fall. Requires Horological Workshops in two of our towns, 3,000 gold, the highest prestige, and Zurich grown into a city of banks and learned societies.

conditions.text: A Horological Workshop stands in at least 2 of our locations
We own Zurich and its development is at least 48

event.title: The Perpetual Republic
event.text:
What the ancient Romans could not achieve (a republic that endures), the Swiss have accomplished. While empires rise and fall around them, the Confederation stands: prosperous, neutral, and free. The Swiss model of governance, where power flows from the people upward through cantonal assemblies, has become an inspiration to political thinkers across Europe.

This pinnacle demands a final choice: embrace constitutional liberalism as a beacon to the world, or consolidate financial power as the quiet architects of European prosperity.

options.text: Let our constitution be a light to all nations

modifiers.name: Liberal Constitution
modifiers.text: The Swiss constitutional model inspires political thinkers across Europe, granting the Confederation diplomatic influence far beyond its size.

modifiers.name: Financial Hegemony
modifiers.text: Swiss banking houses have become the quiet architects of European prosperity, their financial networks spanning the continent.

destiny.name: Gateway to Italy
destiny.text: Cross the Alps and seize the Italian gateway. Bellinzona and Como command the passes into the Lombard plain, the first step toward a Swiss empire south of the mountains. Requires both cities, an army of 30,000, and 1,000 gold.

conditions.text: Own Bellinzona, or a subject owns it
Own Como, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Ticino Falls
event.text:
Swiss pike columns have crossed the Alps and seized the gateway to Italy. Bellinzona's three castles (Castelgrande, Montebello, and Sasso Corbaro) now fly the white cross. Como, that jewel of the Lombard lakes, has been brought under Confederate control.

The Italian princes take notice. The Swiss are no longer content to defend their mountains. They are marching south, and their pikes are as sharp as their ambition.

options.text: Italy lies open before us: the pikes shall lead the way

destiny.name: Lombard Conquest
destiny.text: Dominate the richest plain in Europe. Milano and Brescia (the workshops of Italy) must bow to Swiss arms. Requires both cities, an army of 50,000, high prestige, and 2,000 gold. This stage cannot be completed before the Age of Discovery, when Swiss pike squares took Milan.

conditions.text: Own Milan, or a subject owns it
Own Brescia, or a subject owns it

event.title: Masters of Lombardy
event.text:
Milano has fallen. The richest city in northern Italy (its workshops, its armories, its great cathedral) now answers to Swiss authority. Brescia's renowned arms industry supplies the very weapons that conquered it. The Swiss Confederation has achieved what the Holy Roman Empire spent centuries failing to maintain: firm control over the Lombard plain.

The question now is how to maintain this empire. Train an elite corps of professional Reislaufer, or mobilize the full manpower of every canton?

options.text: Quality over quantity: forge the finest soldiers in Europe

modifiers.name: Elite Reisläufer
modifiers.text: The Swiss have invested in quality over quantity, producing the finest professional infantry in Europe, though domestic construction suffers from the martial focus.

options.text: Every Swiss man is a soldier: mobilize them all

modifiers.name: Mass Mobilization
modifiers.text: Every canton musters its full strength, and mercenary companies flock to the Confederate banner for reduced premiums.

destiny.name: The Greater Helvetic Empire
destiny.text: Forge an empire stretching from the Rhine to the Po. Strasbourg, Verona, and Turin must all fly the white cross. Requires all three cities, an army of 75,000, the highest prestige, and 3,000 gold.

conditions.text: Own Strasbourg, or a subject owns it
Own Verona, or a subject owns it
Own Turin, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Greater Helvetic Empire
event.text:
From Strasbourg on the Rhine to Verona on the Adige, from Turin at the foot of the western Alps to the ancient cantons of the Eidgenossen: the white cross commands an empire that no one believed possible. Swiss pikemen, who once fought only to defend their valleys, now garrison the great cities of Europe.

This is the Switzerland that Marignano never happened to, or rather, the Switzerland that won at Marignano and kept marching. The final question: rule through shock and discipline, or through the glory that draws warriors to your banner?

modifiers.name: Shock and Terror
modifiers.text: Swiss armies strike with devastating speed and reinforce rapidly, though the expense of constant campaigning drives up prices at home.

options.text: Let glory be our recruitment officer

modifiers.name: Glory Seekers
modifiers.text: The legend of Swiss martial prowess draws warriors from across Europe, seeking to fight under the white cross banner.

units.name: Swiss Halberdiers
units.text: Mountain warriors wielding the halberd, a combination weapon of axe, hook, and spike that could pull knights from horseback and crack open armor. Their skill in rough terrain is unmatched.

units.name: Auszug Pikemen
units.text: The first call of the cantonal levy: men picked at the muster, each bringing his own long pike, breastplate and iron helm. Packed into the great column, they broke the knights of Burgundy at Grandson, Murten and Nancy.

units.name: Swiss Crossbowmen
units.text: Alpine marksmen who rain bolts down upon enemies from mountain positions, softening formations before the halberdiers charge.

units.name: Swiss Pike Square
units.text: The Gevierthaufen in miniature, a disciplined block of pikemen trained to hold formation under cavalry charge and artillery fire alike. Their wall of steel points is nearly impenetrable.

units.name: Swiss Musketeer
units.text: Swiss infantry who have adapted to gunpowder warfare while retaining their legendary discipline and mountain-fighting traditions.

units.name: Cantonal Militia
units.text: Citizen-soldiers of the modernized Swiss militia system, combining musket drill with the traditional Swiss fighting spirit. Every man a soldier, every canton a fortress.

units.name: Swiss Sharpshooter
units.text: Elite marksmen from the Swiss shooting tradition, combining precision manufacturing with mountain warfare expertise. Their accuracy at range is devastating.

buildings.name: Letzi Wall
buildings.text: A barrier wall built across an alpine valley or lake approach, designed to channel invaders into prepared defensive positions. The Letzi of the original Forest Cantons could stretch for miles.

buildings.name: Tagsatzung Hall
buildings.text: A hall where cantonal delegates convene to debate and decide federal policy through consensus. The Tagsatzung embodies the Swiss principle that authority flows upward from the people.

buildings.name: Geneva Counting House
buildings.text: A financial institution managing deposits, extending credit, and facilitating the complex web of trade that flows through Switzerland's alpine passes.

buildings.name: Swiss Textile Manufactory
buildings.text: A workshop producing the fine linens and woolens that made St. Gallen, Zurich, and Basel centers of the European textile trade.

buildings.name: Horological Workshop
buildings.text: An atelier where master watchmakers craft intricate timepieces of unparalleled precision, the ultimate expression of Swiss craftsmanship.

buildings.name: Swiss Arsenal
buildings.text: A cantonal weapons stockpile and armory maintaining the arms, ammunition, and equipment needed to mobilize the militia at a moment's notice.

buildings.name: Alpine Hospice
buildings.text: A shelter maintained by religious orders along the great alpine passes, offering care to travelers and pilgrims crossing the mountains.

buildings.name: Swiss Rathaus
buildings.text: A town hall where elected councils govern municipal affairs, the physical embodiment of Swiss republican self-governance.

buildings.name: Schiesstand
buildings.text: A communal shooting range where citizens practice marksmanship, maintaining the military readiness that is every Swiss man's duty.

buildings.name: Dairy Cooperative
buildings.text: An alpine dairy processing facility where herdsmen pool their milk to produce the cheeses that have made Swiss dairy famous across Europe.

where.text: The location's raw material is Livestock

buildings.name: Diplomatic Residence
buildings.text: A neutral ground where foreign envoys meet and negotiations unfold, leveraging Switzerland's reputation for impartiality and discretion.

buildings.name: Sust
buildings.text: The staging warehouse of a pass road. The valley's muleteers carry goods over their own stage and no further, so every bale and barrel rests here overnight, safe from weather and thieves, and pays the transit due that keeps the mule track open.

buildings.name: Swiss Exchange House
buildings.text: A premier financial institution where the wealth of Europe is managed with legendary Swiss discretion: deposits, letters of credit, and currency exchange conducted behind closed doors.

buildings.name: Reisläufer Barracks
buildings.text: A professional military facility where Swiss soldiers are trained in the arts of pike warfare, mountain combat, and the disciplined formations that have made them the terror of European battlefields.

list.name: Tagsatzung
list.text: The Federal Diet of the Old Swiss Confederacy. Each canton sent two delegates, bound by mandate from their home council, to consensus sessions rotating between Baden, Lucerne, Zurich and Frauenfeld, never a permanent capital. From the 15th century until 12 September 1848, when the assembled diet adopted the first Federal Constitution and dissolved itself into the modern bicameral parliament, the Tagsatzung was the working machinery of confederal government: slow, cantonal, structurally allergic to royal authority.

list.name: Stanser Verkommnis
list.text: The Treaty of Stans, concluded 22 December 1481 after the hermit Niklaus von Flue's last-minute mediation saved the Confederacy from civil war between rural and urban cantons over the spoils of the Burgundian Wars. It confirmed the Pfaffenbrief of 1370 and the Sempacherbrief of 1393, banned unauthorized assemblies, regulated the proportional division of conquered land, and obliged the cantons to mutual aid against internal sedition. The institutional spine of self-binding pacts (the Bundesbriefe) that turned a defensive league of three into a coherent thirteen-canton polity.

list.name: Landsgemeinde
list.text: The open-air sovereign assembly of armed citizens, in continuous use in Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden, Glarus, Zug and Appenzell from the 13th and 14th centuries onward. Voters gathered annually on the Landsgemeindeplatz to elect Landammann and judges, ratify the budget, and decide laws by a show of raised hands. Glarus has held its assembly without interruption since 1387 and Appenzell-Innerrhoden since 1403. The most direct form of self-government in early-modern Europe and a permanent structural rebuke to noble jurisdiction.

list.name: Pensionenwesen
list.text: The foreign-service pension system that turned Swiss military prowess into cantonal revenue. After the Treaty of Fribourg in 1516, the cantons institutionalized capitulation contracts with foreign crowns: France, the Papacy, Spain, Savoy, the Dutch Republic and others paid fixed pensions to cantonal treasuries in exchange for the right to recruit Swiss regiments on Swiss soil. By 1740 over 12,000 Swiss served in French pay alone. The pensions kept domestic taxes low, made cantonal elites dependent on foreign princes, and drew clerical condemnation that ran from Zwingli to the late-18th-century reformers who finally abolished the system.

list.name: Gemeine Herrschaften
list.text: The common bailiwicks: subject territories jointly conquered and jointly administered by groups of cantons. The Aargau (1415), the Thurgau (1460), the Rheintal (1490) and the ultramontane bailiwicks south of the Alps (Bellinzona, Lugano, Locarno, Mendrisio and the rest of present-day Ticino) taken from the Duchy of Milan during the Italian Wars. Each was governed by a Landvogt rotated every two years from one of the cosseigneurial cantons. The system extracted revenue from non-cantonal subjects without admitting them to citizenship, funded confederal expenditure, and was bitterly resented by the bailiwick populations until the French abolished it in 1798.

list.name: Zurcher Sittenmandate
list.text: The Zurich Morals Mandates, the corpus of civic-religious legislation passed by the Zurich Rat from Zwingli's reform onward and replicated in Geneva, Basel, Bern and Schaffhausen. Some 400 ordinances issued between 1520 and 1675 regulated swearing, gambling, dress, attendance at sermons, the baptism of newborns, the form of gravestones, the opening hours of taverns, and the conduct of beggars. Enforced by a magistracy that fused city council and consistory, the mandates produced the most disciplined civic populations in Europe and fastened the Reformed church inseparably to the cantonal state.
